en.title: Poland: capital deepening, security-state investment and the next stage of European convergence
en.deck: Poland's next convergence phase depends on turning EU funds, defence spending, energy transition and infrastructure into domestic productivity and technological depth while the population contracts and fiscal commitments rise.
en.regime: Capital-deepening convergence under security pressure: fast growth and high investment coexist with demographic contraction, a coal-to-renewables-and-nuclear transition, large defence commitments and rising dependence on execution quality.
en.key_risk: Security, social and energy-investment commitments expand faster than labour supply and productivity, keeping inflation and financing costs high while raising long-run fiscal pressure.

pt-BR.title: Polônia: aprofundamento de capital, investimento do Estado de segurança e a próxima etapa da convergência europeia
pt-BR.deck: A próxima fase da convergência polonesa depende de transformar fundos europeus, defesa, transição energética e infraestrutura em produtividade e profundidade tecnológica domésticas enquanto a população diminui e compromissos fiscais aumentam.
pt-BR.regime: Convergência por aprofundamento de capital sob pressão de segurança: crescimento e investimento elevados coexistem com contração demográfica, transição carvão-renováveis-nuclear, grandes compromissos de defesa e dependência crescente da qualidade de execução.
pt-BR.key_risk: Compromissos de segurança, sociais e energéticos crescem mais rápido que oferta de trabalho e produtividade, mantendo inflação e custos financeiros altos e elevando pressão fiscal de longo prazo.

selection_rationale: Revision 1 materially deepens the published Poland dossier after editorial review found the first edition too compressed. It adds the post-1989 convergence mechanism, EU capital channels, divided-executive institutional transmission, external trade composition, zloty adjustment, defence industrialisation, dual-use logistics, energy-system integration, regional distribution, domestic ownership and an explicit contradiction ledger while preserving the original country-context ID.
contrary_evidence: Poland's rapid growth, strong manufacturing integration, improving infrastructure and large EU investment flows argue against treating demographic decline or coal dependence as immediate evidence of structural stagnation.

High defence spending and strategic investment do not automatically create domestic productive capacity; imported equipment, inflation, labour scarcity and execution bottlenecks can reduce the growth return.
limitations: 2026 GDP, inflation, trade and fiscal data are provisional and subject to revision.
Defence spending is not equivalent to domestic industrial value added; procurement localisation must be observed separately.
Migration and refugee populations are harder to measure than resident-population estimates and can change quickly.
Nuclear capacity is planned and in preparatory works; it is not operating generation.
RRF headline allocations are financing envelopes; economic effects depend on milestones, absorption, execution and project quality.
